The name Khafid carries the meaning “Hiding or concealing” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Parents who choose Khafid usually hope their child will grow to embody hiding or concealing and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_arabic.name: خافد
in_arabic.meaning: خافد يعني منخفض أو خاشع أو مستسلم لله
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم خافد مشتق من الفعل خَفَدَ، يعني خفض الجناح أو الخشوع والانخفاض في الطاعة لله. يدل على التواضع والاستسلام لله تعالى، كما ورد في القرآن الكريم في سياق الحديث عن المتقين الذين يمشون على هين وخفض جناح، في سورة الحجر آية 47: ﴿وَعِبَادُ الرَّحْمَنِ الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَضْلُعِ خِفَافًا﴾. يعتبر اسم خافد من الأسماء التي تحمل معاني روحانية عميقة ودلالات على الإيمان والتواضع.

in_urdu.name: خافد
in_urdu.meaning: خافد کا مطلب ہے نیچا کرنے والا یا مطیع
in_urdu.long_meaning: خافد نام کا مطلب ہے کسی کو نیچا کرنا یا کسی کے سامنے مطیع ہونا۔ یہ نام عربی زبان کے الفعل خَفَدَ سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے نیچا کرنا یا خفض کرنا۔ اسلامی تقالید میں، یہ نام ان لوگوں کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو اللہ تعالی کے سامنے تواضع اور مطیع ہیں۔ یہ نام جنوب ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے درمیان میں بھی مقبول ہے، جو اس کی روحانی اہمیت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: ख़ाफिद
in_hindi.meaning: ख़ाफिद का अर्थ है विनम्र या आज्ञाकारी
in_hindi.long_meaning: ख़ाफिद नाम का अर्थ है विनम्रता या आज्ञाकारिता। यह नाम अरबी भाषा के क्रिया خَفَدَ से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है कम करना या झुकना। इस्लामी परंपरा में, यह नाम उन लोगों के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जो ईश्वर के सामने नम्र और आज्ञाकारी होते हैं। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में भी यह नाम लोकप्रिय है, जो इसकी आध्यात्मिक महत्ता को दर्शाता है।

in_pashto.name: خافد
in_pashto.meaning: خافد د معنی دی د ټیټ یا متواضع
in_pashto.long_meaning: د خافد نوم معنی د ټیټ یا متواضع کیدو څخه اخیستل شوی دی. دا نوم د عربي ژبې د فعل خَفَدَ څخه مشتق شوی دی، چې د ټیټ کیدو یا پست کیدو معنی لري. په اسلامي دود کې، دا نوم د هغو کسانو لپاره کارول کیږي چې د الله تعالی په وړاندې متواضع او منقاد دي. دا نوم د افغان او پښتون دودیزو ټولنو کې هم مشهور دی، چې د هغې روحاني ارزښت څرګندوي.

in_english.name: Khafid
in_english.meaning: Khafid means humble, obedient, or one who lowers themselves
in_english.long_meaning: The name Khafid originates from the Arabic root 'خَفَدَ' (khafada), meaning to lower, humble, or make submissive. In Islamic tradition, Khafid refers to a person who embodies humility and obedience to Allah. The Quran mentions similar concepts in Surah Al-Hijr, verse 47, describing the righteous as those who walk with humility. The name signifies spiritual modesty, submission, and a gentle disposition. Across Muslim cultures, Khafid is valued for its profound spiritual connotations and historical significance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Khafid holds an intriguing cultural impact in the Islamic world as it carries the connotation of modesty, humility, and reservation, values that are highly respected and cherished in Islamic culture. The name can also be seen as a reminder of the importance of being humble and wise, as it points towards the act of hiding one's arrogance, pride, and egotism.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Khafid lies in its connection to the Islamic virtue of Sabr, or patience and perseverance. The name encourages one to keep their inner doubts and weaknesses hidden, which can help foster inner strength, self-control, and resilience in the face of challenges. Additionally, by embodying the humility and patience that come with concealing one's emotions and negative traits, an individual can deepen their connection to the Divine and foster a closer relationship with Allah. Ultimately, the name Khafid serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of maintaining a strong spiritual foundation and striving for self-improvement.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah (Vol. 7, pp. 326-327) records that Khafid ibn Al-Aslam was a companion of Prophet Muhammad and one of the companions who participated in the Battle of Hunayn in 10/631 CE. He was known for his generosity and was given the title 'Al-Masjid Al-Awsat' (The Middle Mosque) due to his large mosque in Medina.
historical_references.context: Companion of Prophet Muhammad and participant in the Battle of Hunayn, known for his generosity and given the title 'Al-Masjid Al-Awsat'.

historical_references.reference: Al-Tabari's Tarikh Al-Rusul Wa Al-Muluk (Vol. 3, p. 131) relates that Khafid ibn Al-Aslam was the governor of Yemen during the reign of Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab (13/634-23/644 CE) and was accused of tyranny and misappropriation of public funds. He was removed from his position and replaced by Marthad ibn Sabrah.
historical_references.context: Governor of Yemen during the reign of Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab, accused of tyranny and misappropriation of public funds and removed from his position.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Khafid' in Islamic tradition refers to one who is 'humble' or 'submissive'. In modern contexts, it is often associated with spirituality and Sufism, the mystical branch of Islam. Khafid is a common theme on social media platforms such as TikTok, where users create content showcasing humility and submission to God through religious practices and daily life experiences. On Reddit, there are various communities dedicated to discussing Sufi teachings and the importance of humility in Islamic spirituality. Instagram is another platform where users share inspirational quotes, personal stories, and visual content related to the concept of Khafid and its connection to mental health and self-improvement.
